original_value: The double tendon-sheath drive system is widely used in the design of surgical robots and search and rescue robots because of its simplicity, dexterity, and long-distance transmission. We are attempting to apply it to manipulators, wherenon-linear characteristics such as gaps, hysteresis, etc., due to friction between the contact surfaces of the tendon sheath and the flexibility of the rope, are the main difficulties in controlling such manipulators. Most of the existing compensation control methods applicable to double tendon-sheath actuators are offline compensation methods that do not require output feedback, but when the system’s motion and configuration changes, it cannot adapt to the drastic changes in the transmission characteristics. Depending on the transmission system, the robotic arm, changes at any time during the working process, and the force sensors and torque sensors that cannot be applied to the joints of the robot, so a real-time position compensation control method based on flexible cable deformation is proposed. A double tendon-sheath transmission model is established, a double tendon-sheath torque transmission model under any load condition is derived, and a semi-physical simulation experimental platform composed of a motor, a double tendon-sheath transmission system and a single articulated arm is established to verify the transfer model. Through the signal feedback of the end encoder, a real-time closed-loop feedback system was established, thus that the system can still achieve the output to follow the desired torque trajectory under the external interference.

result.paraphrase: The double tendon-sheath drive system is widely used in surgical and search-and-rescue robot design because of its simplicity, dexterity, and long-distance transmission. We are trying to apply it to manipulators, where nonlinear characteristics such as gaps and hysteresis caused by friction between the tendon sheath contact surfaces and rope flexibility make control difficult. Most existing compensation control methods for double tendon-sheath actuators are offline methods that do not require output feedback; however, when system motion and configuration change, they cannot adapt to the sharp changes in transmission characteristics. Since the robotic arm may change at any time during operation and force or torque sensors cannot be applied to the robot joints, a real-time position compensation control method based on flexible cable deformation is proposed. A double tendon-sheath transmission model is established, a torque transmission model for any load condition is derived, and a semi-physical simulation test platform consisting of a motor, a double tendon-sheath transmission system, and a single articulated arm is built to verify the transmission model. Using end-encoder signal feedback, a real-time closed-loop feedback system is created so the system can still make its output follow the desired torque trajectory under external interference.
